description: Create the standalone net48-windows console tool Sentinel.AutoRotate (exe name SentinelAutoRotate.exe) under tools/, add it to Sentinel.sln, and implement the single re-entrant Program.cs with --install/--rotate/--uninstall modes. Fully decoupled from the EDR: no ProjectReference in either direction, no DI/MonitorGroup/detection registration. This feature is independent of FEAT-002 (installer wiring) and must come first because FEAT-002's publish/[Files] paths reference the exe this feature produces.
steps: Create tools/Sentinel.AutoRotate/Sentinel.AutoRotate.csproj: SDK-style Microsoft.NET.Sdk, OutputType=Exe, TargetFramework=net48-windows, Nullable=enable, LangVersion=latest, ImplicitUsings=enable, RootNamespace=Sentinel.AutoRotate, AssemblyName=SentinelAutoRotate, Platforms=AnyCPU;x64. NO <Version> element (tools/ is skipped by build.ps1 version stamping, per Sentinel.MlTrainer). NO ProjectReference. NO PackageReference (all APIs are BCL + P/Invoke). Model TFM/LangVersion/Nullable on src/Sentinel.Service/Sentinel.Service.csproj and src/Sentinel.Core/Sentinel.Core.csproj.

Add the project to Sentinel.sln: insert a Project("{FAE04EC0-301F-11D3-BF4B-00C04F79EFBC}") = "Sentinel.AutoRotate", "tools\Sentinel.AutoRotate\Sentinel.AutoRotate.csproj", "{77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777}" / EndProject block after the Sentinel.MlTrainer block, and add the 4 standard lines for GUID 77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777 to GlobalSection(ProjectConfigurationPlatforms) matching the exact Debug|Any CPU / Release|Any CPU ActiveCfg+Build.0 pattern used by every other project.

Create tools/Sentinel.AutoRotate/Program.cs (optionally also NativeMethods.cs in the same project for P/Invoke). Begin with a header comment documenting the honest purpose and the security tradeoff: keeps a local account password unknown to humans while allowing login/install by rotating it to a strong random value every 10 min + keeping autologon on; this stores a machine-recoverable LSA secret DefaultPassword readable in cleartext by any SYSTEM/admin process (LsaRetrievePrivateData / LSASS dump), defends against humans learning the password and against logon guessing/phishing/reuse but NOT against an attacker who already has local admin, and enables autologon so power-on lands at the desktop. State it NEVER blanks the password.

Implement Main(string[]) returning int, synchronous (no async). Dispatch on arg --install / --rotate / --uninstall; unknown/none prints usage and returns nonzero. Each mode in try/catch; every catch logs to the log file and returns nonzero exit code.

--install (require admin via WindowsPrincipal.IsInRole(Administrator), else log + nonzero): (a) register SYSTEM scheduled task(s) invoking SentinelAutoRotate.exe --rotate with a startup trigger AND a 10-minute repeating trigger, idempotently (delete-then-create via schtasks.exe; schtasks is allowed here per context.json). (b) enable autologon for the target account. (c) set UAC ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=5 at HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System via Microsoft.Win32.Registry (no shelling out for the registry write).

--rotate (runs as SYSTEM): (a) determine target local account via WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId + WTSQuerySessionInformation(WTSUserName), fall back to a configured account-name constant. (b) generate a strong random password >=20 chars with upper+lower+digit+symbol using System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator (NEVER System.Random). (c) set the password via NetUserSetInfo level 1003 (USER_INFO_1003 / usri1003_password); NEVER empty. (d) update autologon so next boot still logs in: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon AutoAdminLogon=1, DefaultUserName, DefaultDomainName=machine name, and store the password as the LSA private secret DefaultPassword via LsaStorePrivateData (NOT the cleartext DefaultPassword registry value). Log actions to %ProgramData%\Sentinel\AutoRotate\autorotate.log (create dir if missing); NEVER log the password value.

--uninstall: delete the scheduled task(s); disable autologon (AutoAdminLogon=0, remove the LSA DefaultPassword secret via LsaStorePrivateData with null/zero-length data); leave the account on its last random password (do NOT blank). Print to stdout that after uninstall the user may need to reset the password via standard Windows tools because it is random.

Add exact P/Invoke signatures: netapi32 NetUserSetInfo + USER_INFO_1003 (CharSet.Unicode); advapi32 LsaOpenPolicy/LsaStorePrivateData/LsaClose/LsaNtStatusToWinError + LSA_UNICODE_STRING + LSA_OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES; kernel32 WTSGetActiveConsoleSessionId; wtsapi32 WTSQuerySessionInformation (WTS_INFO_CLASS.WTSUserName=5) + WTSFreeMemory. Clear signatures, no async.
acceptance_criteria: tools/Sentinel.AutoRotate/Sentinel.AutoRotate.csproj exists, is net48-windows OutputType=Exe with AssemblyName=SentinelAutoRotate, has NO ProjectReference and NO <Version> element.
Sentinel.sln contains the Sentinel.AutoRotate project with GUID 77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777 and its 4 ProjectConfigurationPlatforms lines.

Program.cs implements the three modes with the documented header, uses RandomNumberGenerator (not System.Random), NetUserSetInfo (not 'net user'), LsaStorePrivateData for DefaultPassword, never blanks or logs the password, returns nonzero on failure, and every catch logs.
The full solution builds in Debug with 0 errors.
No new test failures beyond the 2 known pre-existing TlsCertificateMonitorTests failures.

& "C:\Program Files\dotnet\dotnet.exe" test e:\Gorstak\Sentinel\.worktrees\autorotate/tests/Sentinel.Tests/Sentinel.Tests.csproj  -> no new failures beyond the 2 pre-existing TlsCertificateMonitorTests failures
findings:
Implemented. Exe output path (Debug): tools/Sentinel.AutoRotate/bin/Debug/net48-windows/SentinelAutoRotate.exe; Release publish target expected at publish/autorotate/SentinelAutoRotate.exe. AssemblyName=SentinelAutoRotate (no <Version>). Files created: tools/Sentinel.AutoRotate/Sentinel.AutoRotate.csproj, Program.cs, NativeMethods.cs. Sln GUID 77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777 added with 4 ProjectConfigurationPlatforms lines.

For FEAT-002 (installer):
- Fallback account-name constant: "Sentinel" (Program.FallbackAccountName). If the installer should pre-create or target a specific account, align it to this name (or the installer must create a local account named Sentinel).
- Scheduled task names: "SentinelAutoRotateStartup" (ONSTART trigger) and "SentinelAutoRotate" (every 10 minutes, /SC MINUTE /MO 10). Both run as SYSTEM /RL HIGHEST and invoke "<exe>" --rotate. --install creates both (delete-then-create idempotent); --uninstall deletes both.
- CLI modes: --install (admin-required; registers tasks, enables autologon, sets UAC ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=5), --rotate (SYSTEM; rotates password + refreshes autologon), --uninstall (removes tasks + disables autologon, leaves password random). Unknown/no arg prints usage and returns exit code 2; failures return nonzero (1).
- Log file: %ProgramData%\Sentinel\AutoRotate\autorotate.log (never logs the password).
- Autologon secret stored as LSA private data "DefaultPassword" via LsaStorePrivateData (NOT the cleartext registry value). Winlogon regkeys set: AutoAdminLogon, DefaultUserName, DefaultDomainName=machine name.
- net48 notes: used RandomNumberGenerator.Create()+GetBytes (net48 has no RandomNumberGenerator.Fill) and Process.MainModule.FileName (net48 has no Environment.ProcessPath).

Verification: full solution Debug build = 0 errors; dotnet test = Failed 2 / Passed 2565 / Total 2567 — the 2 failures are the known pre-existing TlsCertificateMonitorTests, no new failures. Decoupling kept absolute: no ProjectReference/PackageReference, not referenced by or registered in any EDR project.
